name: Egyptian Crowns
description: Egyptian Crowns was a predominantly Black street gang based in the Tremont and Simpson Street areas of the Bronx, New York, active during the late 1950s. They were one of the two main gangs in a Bronx coalition known as the 'Crown nation,' alongside the Valiant Crowns; smaller affiliated gangs included the Bohemian Crowns, Mafia Crowns, Seven Crowns, and Royal Crowns, with the alliance reportedly claiming around 800 members in total. The gang also operated under the guise of a Social Athletic Club (SAC) called the Seven Masters. The Egyptian Crowns gained notoriety in April 1958 when their president, Ramón Serra, was arrested for the shotgun killing of rival Michael Ramos during a conflict with the Sinners gang.
